clue.text: What a skilled labourer does, after removing last of fat below sink initially

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for fat is taken away

parts.note: plump means fat, well-rounded

indicators.note: only the first letters of below and sink are wanted

explanation.surface: A tradesman's routine described as skimming grease off something under the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing last of' cuts PLUMP to PLUM; 'initially' gives B and S from 'below sink'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber is a skilled tradesman, and what such a worker does with pipes is to fit or repair them.

clue.text: Slow movement of mostly fat, round figure

indicators.note: most of the word for fat is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: large means big or fat
the round figure is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Sounds like a description of a portly, rotund person moving slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like physical motion, but it is a section of a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a largo is a piece or section played very slowly and broadly.

clue.text: Space traveller encountered door that is broken

parts.note: met means encountered

indicators.note: the letters of door plus the abbreviation are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An astronaut meets a door that turns out to be broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space traveller' suggests an astronaut, but the traveller is a rock; the 'that is' abbreviation joins the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteoroid is a small rocky body travelling through space, a cosmic traveller rather than a human one.

clue.text: Walked through wild Dorset

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of Dorset running loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A hiker tramps across the untamed Dorset countryside, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of stride: to have walked with long purposeful steps.

clue.text: Daily dash that's made by postman?

parts.note: the Daily Mail is a British newspaper, often called just the Mail
a drop or dash is a small amount, as of milk in tea

explanation.surface: The postman's daily rush on his round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' with its capital stands for the British tabloid, the Daily Mail; 'dash' is a small quantity, as in a dash of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery point where letters are left is something a postal worker makes on the round, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Page to study, when understanding former time period has caused unwanted fat

indicators.note: split as under-standing: in a down answer the page and study pieces stand beneath the period

parts.note: the medieval era is a past period of history
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: Studying history has led someone to put on unwanted weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understanding' is read as 'under standing': P + READ is placed below MIDDLE AGES in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the paunch that tends to develop around the waist in one's forties and fifties.

clue.text: Wanderer's on phone still

parts.note: Wanderer is the setter, so Wanderer's means I'm, the setter is
a mobile is a cellphone

explanation.surface: The setter is still on the phone, as if chatting endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym: 'Wanderer's' = I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still is motionless, not moving at all.

clue.text: 100 paras content to land in Arkansas

indicators.note: content as in contents: the word sits inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: A hundred paratroopers held ready to touch down in Arkansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paras' looks like paratroopers but is the small coin, para; 'content' hides the answer across 'lanD IN ARkansas'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yugoslav and Serbian currency unit was divided into one hundred smaller coins called paras.

clue.text: Like a mother hen, getting some macho VIP aroused

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A protective mother figure stirred up by a macho celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen lays eggs, and egg-laying animals are described by this zoological adjective.

clue.text: Rita the singer, model or public speaker

parts.note: Rita Ora is a British pop singer
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of possible jobs: pop star, fashion model or speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Model T Ford supplies T.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is someone who makes formal speeches in public.

clue.text: Mad teen stupidly swallows one, making trouble for older relative?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take the next piece inside them
the letters of the phrase are put together stupidly, in a jumbled order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A daft teenager gulps something down and so causes grief for a grandparent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges MADTEEN into DEMENTA; 'swallows' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A decline in memory and reasoning is a condition that often afflicts elderly people, hence a trouble for an older relative.

clue.text: Like a doughnut or two, perhaps? Not with one lentil dish

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be arranged another way
not with means the abbreviation for with is left out of the jumble

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
dal is an Indian dish of lentils

explanation.surface: Someone orders a doughnut or two, but not with the lentil curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not with' removes W from OR TWO; 'perhaps' rearranges the remaining ORTO into TORO.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is a ring shape, so a ring-shaped doughnut has this geometric form.

clue.text: Office desk

definitions.meaning: a government department or agency office, as in a travel or news agency
a writing desk with drawers and a sloping lid

explanation.surface: Bare words for a workplace and its furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an administrative department and a writing desk, the room taking its name from the furniture.

clue.text: Backbone shown by circular letter writer

parts.note: read as back-bone: bone gives rib, written back to front
the round letter is O

explanation.surface: A writer shows backbone in a letter sent round to many people.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Backbone' as 'back bone': RIB turned backwards gives BIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A biro is a ballpoint pen, a writing instrument rather than an author.

clue.text: Dead fashionable soulmate after losing mother

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: the word for mother is taken out of the soul-plus-mate pieces

parts.note: split as soul plus mate: soul is anima, then mate
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A trendy soulmate is gone for good after a bereavement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soulmate' must be split: anima is Latin (and Jungian) for soul, then mate; 'after losing' takes out mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without life or movement, like a stone, is lifeless in the same way a corpse is.

clue.text: Washing a lion, tub gets smashed

indicators.note: the letters are smashed to pieces and reassembled

explanation.surface: Bathing a lion goes badly and the tub is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablutions are the act of washing oneself, a formal word for a wash.

clue.text: Toy boy, easily aroused, really starts to go after lingerie

indicators.note: the picked letters are placed after the underwear piece

parts.note: a teddy is a one-piece undergarment for women

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of the four words are used

explanation.surface: A toy boy lover is easily excited by lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy boy' looks like one phrase; 'Toy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed bear is a classic soft toy for children.

clue.text: One having the balls to compete with wife in survey

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: Someone brave enough to take on his wife in an opinion poll.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey is a broad look at a subject, a general summary of it.

clue.text: Spirit of English vaudeville only apparent after sinking first very large double?

indicators.note: sinking means those letters go down, out of the music-hall word
first means the opening letter of very is the one used
double means the letter is taken twice

parts.note: l is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A boozy music-hall show where a big drink is downed first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very large double' is read as V (first of very) and a doubled L for large; 'after sinking' sends both out of the music-hall word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie is a clear fruit brandy, a strong distilled drink.

clue.text: Daughter is 100 — it might be a record

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A daughter reaches a hundred, a record age.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl record is a flat round disc, one example of the word.

clue.text: Highest point of a river — source of Ganges

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
the first letter of Ganges, spelt out as the name of the letter

explanation.surface: The highest point of a river is where the Ganges begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of Ganges is written as its name, GEE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apogee is the furthest point of an orbit, hence a peak or climax.

clue.text: One that freeloads, finally paying and cross about that

indicators.note: about means the hybrid animal goes round that letter

parts.note: a liger is the cross of a lion and a tiger

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of paying

explanation.surface: A freeloader finally pays up and gets annoyed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is the hybrid LIGER. A ligger is British slang for someone who gatecrashes free events.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a hanger-on who attends parties and launches for the free food and drink.

clue.text: What setter might do, having become larger at 50

parts.note: to grow is to become larger
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A crossword setter getting bigger at the age of fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish or English setter is a breed of dog, and a dog might snarl menacingly.

clue.text: Kind of fat, one's beginning to hear, like a young setter

parts.note: puppy fat is the plumpness of childhood
one's means one is, written I'S

indicators.note: the beginning letter of hear is used

explanation.surface: A setter overhears talk of puppy fat and youthful looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'setter' is the dog breed; 'one's' = I'S (one is).
explanation.definitionFit: A young dog is a puppy, so playful youthful behaviour is described this way.

clue.text: After getting up, girl eats one source of fibre

indicators.note: in a down answer getting up reads the letters from bottom to top
the girl takes the numeral inside her

parts.note: a lass is a girl
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A girl rises and eats a high-fibre breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' puts I inside LASS (LAISS); 'getting up' turns it over to give SISAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is an agave plant whose leaves provide a stiff fibre used for rope.

clue.text: Lean lion possibly getting fat

indicators.note: possibly signals another possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A scrawny lion might be fattening up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanoline is the greasy wax obtained from sheep's wool, used in ointments.

clue.text: Fat? Agrees, sadly

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are badly ordered and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sadly concedes that they are overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is animal fat or other oily matter, so it is one kind of fat.

clue.text: What old newspaper might have done, if Scottish island outstanding

definitions.text: What old newspaper might have done

parts.note: Yell is one of the Shetland Islands, north of Scotland
an outstanding debt is one still owed

explanation.surface: Odd speculation about an old paper and an excellent Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like 'excellent' but means unpaid, OWED.
explanation.definitionFit: Old newsprint turns a dingy brownish colour with age.

clue.text: Signs up to see opening of Sophia Loren play

indicators.note: play means the letters move about freely into a new order
the opening letter of Sophia is used

explanation.surface: Fans sign up to see Sophia Loren's opening night in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' is the anagram signal, not a stage show; Sophia Loren is an Italian film star.
explanation.definitionFit: To register oneself as a member or student is to sign on, or sign up.
